incidents.victim: US Water Utilities and Critical Infrastructure (100+ entities)
incidents.vector: IRGC Cyber-Electronic Command directed multiple proxy hacking groups against US water utilities, government agencies, and critical infrastructure using known device vulnerabilities and default credentials
incidents.impact: 100+ water and wastewater utilities across 12 US states breached since late July 2026; US State Department posted $10M reward for IRGC-CEC director Amir Yaryab; Treasury sanctioned Turkish bank Golden Global Bank for facilitating IRGC financial operations

incidents.vector: Public release of three privilege escalation exploits targeting widely deployed antimalware products: Falcon Flank (CrowdStrike), Hard Breacher (Kaspersky), and Pretty Prague (Avast)
incidents.impact: Publicly available exploits enable local privilege escalation by abusing the elevated kernel-level privileges inherent to antimalware products; organizations relying on these endpoint security tools are exposed; no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation reported yet

incidents.vector: Breach of Trezor's unnamed third-party shipping fulfillment provider
incidents.impact: 67,000 additional US customers exposed (names, email, phone, shipping address) for orders placed November 2019 through August 2021; widens a breach first disclosed in August 2026

incidents.vector: Two zero-days chained for unauthenticated RCE: CVE-2026-83548 (max-severity pre-auth SSRF abusing front-end proxy to bypass internal API authentication) and CVE-2026-83549 (OS command injection executed once authenticated)
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed prior to patching; CISA added both CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 3; SonicWall SMA 1000 has accumulated five actively exploited vulnerabilities since late 2025; patches released September 2

incidents.victim: US and Canadian Courts (12+ states, Ontario, US Virgin Islands)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Thomson Reuters C-Track court case management platform; breach undetected from March through June 30, 2026
incidents.impact: Sealed court records, SSNs, driver's license numbers, medical information, dates of birth, and health insurance data exposed across appellate courts in 12+ US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Ontario Canada; Thomson Reuters notified affected courts weeks after its own discovery

incidents.victim: Serbian Opposition Politicians, Activists, and Student Protesters
incidents.vector: Pegasus zero-click spyware delivered remotely via iMessage exploit chain; NoviSpy spyware installed directly on devices during police detentions and phone confiscations
incidents.impact: At least 14 confirmed victims including an MP, a local government official, and student pro-democracy activists targeted since December 2025; infections timed to coincide with March 2026 local elections; Citizen Lab confirmed Pegasus zero-click infections; EU Parliament members called for slowdown of Serbia's EU accession

incidents.victim: US Federal Agencies, Senate, Hospitals, Telecoms, Financial Institutions
incidents.vector: QScan (distributed IoT vulnerability scanning and target database) and QTRouter (covert traffic relay through compromised IoT devices) operated by private firm Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology on behalf of China's MSS and PLA
incidents.impact: US DOJ disrupted both platforms; FBI/NSA joint advisory confirmed targets included US federal agencies, the Senate, hospitals, telecoms, and financial institutions; the operator has supported Chinese government cyber operations for nearly a decade since at least 2018

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to ATF's CALEA (Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act) lawful interception system
incidents.impact: Qilin ransomware group published 6.3 GB of data including law enforcement case folders, investigation target names, phone numbers, IP addresses, and mobile device forensic data; ATF Director Robert Cekada confirmed the agency is investigating the breach

incidents.victim: US and Canadian Identity Verification Sector (153M+ individuals)
incidents.vector: Long-term breach of a Louisiana-based identity verification company whose systems hold biometric scans of government IDs collected at Hertz rental locations, cannabis dispensaries, and other Fortune 500 customer touchpoints
incidents.impact: 153 million+ US and Canadian driver's license images — including infrared and UV scans — now sold on darknet marketplace "Nexus"; data includes government officials including the US Defense Secretary; breach active for over a year and adding roughly 400,000 records per day; FBI New Orleans field office opened investigation

incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) of McKesson employees to steal credentials, followed by use of stolen credentials to take over Okta SSO accounts and exfiltrate patient records at scale
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters group claims 284 million patient records stolen; the same group breached bank IT provider Jack Henry using an identical vishing and Okta-credential-theft playbook the same week

incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) attack to gain network access; internal documents stolen and ransom demand issued
incidents.impact: More than 7,200 bank and financial institution customers notified of breach; Jack Henry refused to pay ransom; ShinyHunters claimed responsibility using the same credential-theft methodology deployed against McKesson

incidents.vector: Mass automated password recovery attack targeting hundreds of thousands of X accounts, believed aimed at pivoting to the X Money digital banking service
incidents.impact: Attack mitigated by X before account takeovers occurred; no confirmed compromises or financial theft; US Attorney General confirmed DOJ is investigating; incident highlights the expanded attack surface introduced by X Money

incidents.vector: Compromise of Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure to inject malicious Terraform module registry servers live for 14 hours on August 31
incidents.impact: Developers using Coder's cloud-infrastructure tooling were served malicious Terraform modules during the window; any cloud environments provisioned via Coder during that period may be compromised

incidents.vector: Attackers registered Lenovo ID accounts using the same email addresses as existing Dropbox accounts, bypassed Lenovo's email verification, then exploited the cross-service integration to access the corresponding Dropbox accounts
incidents.impact: Approximately 5,000 Dropbox accounts accessed and data downloaded; breach disclosed September 4, 2026

incidents.vector: Unauthorized intrusion into TVING's systems at the start of June; the company failed to meet regulatory disclosure deadlines
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 40 million user accounts stolen, including 70+ categories of information such as names, email addresses, and phone numbers; company offered roughly $15 compensation per user in streaming credits and faces regulatory fines for late disclosure

incidents.victim: Mexican Government Agencies and Brazilian Financial Institutions
incidents.vector: Two parallel campaigns using large language models (Claude, GPT-4.1) hosted on attacker-controlled NextChat infrastructure to generate and debug intrusion scripts, combined with living-off-the-land techniques, custom RATs, and SOCKS5 proxies
incidents.impact: Mexico: federal transport ministry, water utilities in Mexico and Ecuador, and federal agencies compromised; Brazil: financial sector organizations breached with data exfiltrated; both campaigns ongoing since February 2026 and represent the first confirmed operational use of AI tools to assist active intrusions in Latin America
